summary: Validated Phase 3b GitHub App downstream sweep (15-file fix). Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_iter363_phase3b_github_app_dispatch.py with 15 tests covering (a) get_repo_token dispatch contract (4 unit tests, mocked), (b) 7 App-installed happy-path endpoints against a synthetic Mongo project (auth_method='github_app', installation_id=99999999, github_token=None), and (c) 4 PAT regression endpoints against a synthetic PAT project. All 15/15 passed. Also re-ran the pre-existing 64/64 GitHub App suite (test_github_app_service.py, test_github_app_router.py, test_github_app_project_add.py) — still fully green after the sweep. NO PAT-missing/no_github_pat/github_credentials_missing errors were returned for the App-installed project on any of the tested endpoints; downstream 401/404 from GitHub are the expected acceptable outcome (fake installation_id).

critical.issue: The cto_projects.find_one projection is `{_id:0, github_owner:1, github_repo:1, github_token:1, name:1}` — MISSING auth_method, installation_id, AND user_id. Passing this incomplete dict into get_repo_token(proj) silently defaults auth_method to 'pat' and calls _decrypt_pat(proj.get('user_id') or '', proj.get('github_token')). For App-installed projects (github_token=None) this returns None and heal falls back to OAuth only — installation-token mint is UNREACHABLE. For encrypted-PAT projects (v1:*), the empty user_id makes the vault decrypt fail. This defeats the sweep's promise for auto-heal on App-installed projects.

Projection includes auth_method BUT MISSING installation_id and user_id. Result: for App-installed projects the admin BIN Tracker PAT-probe sees auth_method='github_app' but installation_id is undefined → get_repo_token returns None → status column silently falls back to oauth_fallback or 'missing'. Cosmetic-severity on the admin dashboard, but a projection-completeness violation of the sweep's own contract.

minor.issue: The `if self.bin_ctx is None:` fallback projection at line 2776-2777 is `{_id:0, github_owner:1, github_repo:1, github_branch:1, github_token:1}` — MISSING auth_method, installation_id, user_id. This is the legacy-only path (bin_ctx is now expected mandatory) so it fires rarely, but if a loop session was rehydrated cross-worker without bin_ctx, App-installed projects would fail SHIP silently.

action_items: Add `auth_method:1, installation_id:1, user_id:1` to the projection in services/repo_heal.py:174-175 (heal_project function).
Add `installation_id:1, user_id:1` to the projection in routers/admin_bin.py:88-91 (bin_tracker_projects function).
Add `auth_method:1, installation_id:1, user_id:1` to the SHIP-fallback projection in services/loop_engine.py:2776-2777 (SHIP `_do_ship` `if self.bin_ctx is None` branch).
critical_code_review_comments: The 15-file sweep is correct in principle and passes end-to-end on the tested endpoints (repo-status, codebase-health/scan, security-scan, user-rollback, loop/rollback, mcp/projects, admin/brain-replay) for BOTH synthetic App-installed and PAT projects.

3 projections were flagged as incomplete (see backend_issues above) — the endpoint tests still passed on the FIRST two because they don't hit those specific code paths on the synthetic project without a matching prior loop run, but the projection contract is broken and will regress for real users.

get_repo_token dispatch is now unit-locked (4 tests) — future refactors that break github_app vs pat vs legacy semantics will fail CI. Recommend main agent moves this test into the permanent regression suite.

loop_engine.py plan-phase (line 537) and SHIP main-path bin_ctx branch use bin_ctx.pat directly — that path was NOT changed by this sweep. If bin_ctx.pat is populated via a code path that doesn't dispatch on auth_method, App-installed loop runs may still PAT-fail. Worth main-agent audit of BINContext construction (services/bin_context.py line 192) to confirm it uses get_repo_token for App-installed projects.
seed_data_creation: Created 2 synthetic cto_projects docs per test module (auto-teardown in fixtures): TEST_appinst_<uuid>* (auth_method=github_app, installation_id=99999999, github_token=None) and TEST_pat_<uuid>* (auth_method=pat, github_token=ghp_fake). Both deleted after tests complete.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file lives at /app/backend/tests/test_iter363_phase3b_github_app_dispatch.py — reusable regression for future GitHub App sweep changes. The 3 projection bugs found are cosmetic-to-medium severity and do NOT block prod deploy of the sweep (real customer's blocking codepath — chat.py, loop.py, user_rollback.py, codebase_health.py, security_scan.py, admin.py, repo_status.py, mcp.py — all have correct projections and passed both happy-path and regression). Main agent should apply the 3 projection fixes as a follow-up patch.
rca of the issue: Sweep root cause: 15 callsites were calling `_decrypt_pat(user_id, proj.get('github_token'))` directly, bypassing the github_app dispatch. Fix pattern: replace with `await get_repo_token(proj)` from services.pat_vault + expand each Mongo projection to include auth_method/installation_id/user_id. Verified with 15 tests that 8 out of the 8 tested endpoints on the customer-blocking path no longer PAT-gate an App-installed project. Remaining 3 projection gaps in repo_heal.py, admin_bin.py, and loop_engine.py:2777 (SHIP fallback) do NOT affect the customer's active-workflow blocker; they are follow-up hardening.
